messages.author: 7e01961f1f4ce874
messages.subject: Equijoin - join key as dataframe
parts:
Hi Antonio,

We have a requirement of joining two data sets on composite key (multiple columns), for this purpose we thought of creating join keys as data frame, it didn't work.
But if we create join key by using paste(columns) it works fine, even data frame with single column works fine. What is the ideal way of forming joinkey in case of composite key. 

a <- head(mtcars, n=10)
b <- tail(mtcars, n=5)
a <- cbind(a, data.frame(c=1:10, d = letters[1:10], stringsAsFactors=FALSE))
b <- cbind(b, data.frame(c=1:5,  d = letters[1:5],  stringsAsFactors=FALSE))
hdfs.rm('a.data')
to.dfs(a,'a.data')
hdfs.rm('b.data')
to.dfs(b,'b.data')
adata = mapreduce(map=function(k,v) (keyval(data.frame(joinKey1=v$c, joinKey2=v$d, stringsAsFactors=FALSE), v)),input='a.data')
bdata = mapreduce(map=function(k,v) (keyval(data.frame(joinKey1=v$c, joinKey2=v$d, stringsAsFactors=FALSE), v)),input='b.data')
merged.data.path = equijoin (left.input = adata, right.input = bdata)
merged.data = from.dfs(merged.data.path) # got 7 records I was expecting 5

Thanks 
Abhishek

messages.subject: Re: Equijoin - join key as dataframe
parts:
I will look into this. I am not sure what you mean by "ideal" but this is should be supported. Thanks for putting together simple reproducible test cases. The only thing that looks odd is that you insist in discarding the return value of to.dfs and make up file names that you then need to copy and paste around. That's  not related to this problem, just noticing an rmr feature you are not using. Best is submitting a bug report in the rmr2 issue tracker, if it's not a bug we'll close it,  no harm done. Here on the group there are no features for me to track what is still in need of attention and what has been addressed. Thanks

Antonio
